claim: Traffic signals adapt through local feedback of queue length and vehicle count, adjusting green time to minimize local waiting time
mechanism: Each intersection continuously monitors its own queue length and vehicle count, then adjusts signal timing proportionally to reduce local waiting times without considering downstream effects
evidence: Local traffic sensors can provide real-time queue length data
Some adaptive signal systems use local queue detection
assumptions: Local optimization leads to global optimization
Queue length is the primary determinant of system performance
expected_failure_modes: Braess paradox where local improvements create system-wide congestion
Inability to coordinate platoon movement between intersections
novelty_rationale: Applies the myxomycete principle of local resource optimization to traffic signals without requiring central coordination
testability: Can be tested in simulation by comparing local-only optimization with centralized optimization
falsifier: If implementing local-only optimization results in increased delays at downstream intersections or causes gridlock at network scale
